t:
That the second paragraph of section 215 of title 17, United States Code, is amended by striking out the period at the end thereof, inserting a colon in lieu thereof, and adding the following new provisions:

“And provided farther, That with respect to works of foreign origin, in lieu of payment of the copyright fee of $4 together with one copy of the work and application, the foreign author or proprietor may at any time within six months from the date of first publication abroad deposit in the Copyright Office an application for registration and two copies of the work which shall be accompanied by a catalog card in form and content satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights.”

fable.w: The section only lets a foreign author or proprietor register a copyright by depositing an application, two copies of the work and a catalog card instead of paying the fee. The tempting reading is that an outside party is dealing with a federal office, with the card to be 'satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights', but this is an application for registration, which the definition excludes. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: the foreign author or proprietor may at any time within six months from the date of first publication abroad deposit in the Copyright Office an application for registration and two copies of the work

qwen_block.w: This section describes the procedure for a foreign author to apply for copyright registration by depositing an application and copies of the work. The definition explicitly states that 'applications for benefits or grants' are not participation. Here, the outside party (foreign author) is applying for a legal right (copyright registration), which falls under the exclusion for applications. There is no consultation, advisory board, public hearing, or right to sue involved in this specific text.
qwen_block.s: the foreign author or proprietor may at any time within six months from the date of first publication abroad deposit in the Copyright Office an application for registration and two copies of the work which shall be accompanied by a catalog card in form and content satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights.

opus.w: This provision lets foreign authors apply for copyright registration in a different way, and applications for registrations or licenses are excluded from participation. The outside party is not being consulted on a federal policy decision. The phrase "satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights" sets what form the Register will accept; it does not require or authorize rulemaking, comment periods, or consultation.
opus.s: the foreign author or proprietor may at any time within six months from the date of first publication abroad deposit in the Copyright Office an application for registration and two copies of the work
opus.b:
**Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting reading is that a foreign author, who is outside the federal government, deals directly with the Copyright Office. It also mentions a catalog card "in form and content satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights," which could look like a grant of rulemaking power. Neither holds up. Depositing an application and copies of a work is applying for a registration, which the definition excludes. The "satisfactory to the Register" wording describes what the Register must accept. It does not authorize regulations or provide for any comment or consultation.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the procedure for registering a copyright, which is an application process. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' The requirement that the catalog card be 'satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights' is a standard for acceptance of the application, not a consultation or coordination with an outside party before a federal decision. The foreign author is applying for a registration, not participating in the government's decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: the foreign author or proprietor may at any time within six months from the date of first publication abroad deposit in the Copyright Office an application for registration and two copies of the work which shall be accompanied by a catalog card in form and content satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the catalog card to be "satisfactory to the Register of Copyrights" implies a consultation or feedback loop with the applicant (an outside party). However, this is merely a standard for acceptance of an application, not a participatory process in decision-making. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" (and by extension, registrations/licenses) from participation. The interaction is purely administrative and unilateral (submitting a form that meets criteria), not a consultation or coordination before a federal decision in the policy or advisory sense.
